current.text: He is a rookie, taken No. 4 overall by the Bulls.
He is in the projected Bulls starting five with Josh Giddey, Norman Powell, Matas Buzelis and Nic Claxton.
The Bulls are giving him a lot of usage, while the usage rates of Giddey and Buzelis are down.
Experts expect him to be the second-best rookie this season.
Experts call a pick in the 80s a fair price and take him around picks 86 to 89. His ESPN rank in the 50s and 60s is too high.
Not all experts are comfortable with him. One is uneasy taking him at pick 84 and another has avoided him because of the rookie uncertainty.
Expect rough moments and shaky efficiency early. His early value should come from defensive stats.
In summer league he took many threes, about 8 a game, and averaged 22 points and 7 rebounds on 37% usage. His shooting fell off as summer league went on.
His summer league shooting is partly fool's gold. He may shoot only about 30 percent from three this season.
Pairing him with Zach Edey on a fantasy roster takes away much of his upside.
Nikola Vucevic and Coby White have left Chicago, which frees up usage for the young players.
New head coach Tiago Splitter replaces Billy Donovan and is expected to push young players out of their comfort zones.
The Bulls project as a bad team. The team lacks shooting, and a lineup with Claxton, Wilson and Giddey will have poor spacing.
The Bulls should play a fast, up-tempo transition style.
The Bulls play 10 games in our fantasy playoff weeks (3-3-4) and have 15 back-to-backs.

durable.text: His fantasy value comes from rebounds, blocks and steals. Blocks and rebounds are his best categories for a forward.
Shooting is his weak point. He is a poor free throw shooter, and his three-point shot is a concern.
He is a good finisher and athlete.
He is not a passer and has tunnel vision. Assists are not part of his value.
He was a low-usage player in college and entered the NBA seen as a defensive prospect.
Long term he should lean more defensive than offensive, though the gap should narrow.
He is worth more in category leagues than in points leagues, because his defensive stats count less in points formats.

note: Experts take him around picks 86 to 89. With 144 players drafted, that makes him a mid-to-late auction target near his Yahoo average cost of 4.0 USD and ESPN's 6.4 USD. Do not chase him at ESPN's rank 57. His rebounds, blocks (z +1.8 vs forwards) and steals help teams that need frontcourt defensive stats, and his weak FT% (74.7%) and assists hurt least in builds that already give those up. Early in the season, check whether the Bulls keep feeding him usage under Splitter, how many threes he takes, and whether his efficiency settles.
